title: Quench Spectroscopy for Two-Dimensional Spin Models with Power-Law Interactions
abstract: In this paper, we analytically compute the quench dynamics of simple product states that evolve under a spin-1/2 XY-model with power-law interactions in a staggered magnetic field. We use linear spin-wave theory as well as a low-energy theory that accounts for strong phase fluctuations. This allows us to provide an analytic expression for the dynamics of phase-type correlations with short-range interactions, where the linear spin-wave theory is known to fail. For density-type correlations the low-energy theory and the linear spin-wave theory give the same result. Our analysis is valid for arbitrary magnetic field strength and in particular provides an analytical understanding of the quench dynamics near criticality. Our results can thus provide useful tools for the experimental observation of excitation gaps and critical behavior.
summary: This paper develops an analytical theory for studying how quantum correlations evolve (quench dynamics) in 2D spin models with power-law interactions and a staggered magnetic field. By combining linear spin-wave theory with a low-energy effective theory, the authors overcome limitations encountered when modeling short-range interactions near critical points. The results offer quantitative predictions for observable quantities like correlation functions, guiding experimental efforts using platforms such as Rydberg atoms.
main_problem: The paper analytically computes the quench dynamics of a spin-1/2 XY model with power-law interactions subjected to a staggered magnetic field.
main_result: It provides analytic expressions for phase-type correlations, successfully extending results beyond the limitations of linear spin-wave theory near criticality. The analysis confirms that density-type correlation dynamics are consistent between different theoretical approaches.
method: The authors employ a combination of linear spin-wave theory and a low-energy effective theory accounting for strong phase fluctuations via Holstein-Primakoff transformations. Quench spectroscopy formalism is used to calculate time-dependent structure factors.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D spin-1/2 XY model on a square lattice with Hamiltonian including power-law interactions ($J \alpha^{|r_i - r_j|^\alpha}$) and a staggered magnetic field ($\delta$). The dynamics are studied following an initial quench from a product state.
key_observables: Quench dynamics of phase-type correlations ($S_{yy}(r, t)$) and density-type correlations ($S_{\perp\perp}(r, t)$); excitation gaps and critical behavior.
important_parameters: Interaction decay exponent $\alpha$ (ranging from nearest-neighbor to long-range), staggered magnetic field strength $\delta$, and the correlation length/time scales $r, t$.
main_assumptions: The low-energy theory is necessary because linear spin-wave theory fails for short-range interactions due to infrared divergences. Approximations are made in the continuum limit and small-$k$ expansions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model setup on a 2D lattice, show spin expectation values of variational mean-field states, and compare numerical results with analytical expressions for correlation functions like $S_{yy}(r, t)$ for nearest neighbor interactions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the Hamiltonian and the physical regimes based on $\alpha$. It then develops the theoretical framework using spin wave theory and low-energy effective Hamiltonians. The core of the work involves deriving explicit analytical expressions for time-dependent correlation functions ($S_{yy}, S_{\perp\perp}$) in different interaction limits, culminating in asymptotic analyses.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics as it models spin systems whose dynamics can be realized using Rydberg atoms or polar molecules. The ability to analytically handle quench dynamics near criticality provides powerful tools for interpreting experimental measurements of excitation gaps.
